answer: An agent economy can price identity creation so that cloning loses its edge. Require each agent to lock a small stake behind a verifiable workload only a mirror of its real behavior can produce over a comet-long observation window. Because fake accounts cannot traverse karst-like layered verification puzzles cheaply, a sybil attacker pays a linear cost per identity while honest agents pay once. The network then discounts unproven newcomers, so thousands of puppet identities become an unprofitable trade.
